solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument of torture little Tom's gang used

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so little Tom's gives his surname plus the S of the possessive
a crew is a gang of people working or going about together

explanation.surface: A torture device that a little lad called Tom and his gang made use of.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folklore; 'used' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This device crushed a victim's digits in a vice, a classic implement of medieval and early-modern torment.

clue.text: Worked in garden before private dance

indicators.note: before places the gardening word ahead of the word for private in the answer

parts.note: to hoe is to work the soil with a garden hoe, so worked in garden gives the past tense
own means private, belonging to oneself, as in 'my own room'

explanation.surface: Someone did some gardening and then went off to a private dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American country dance or social gathering featuring square dancing goes by this name.

clue.text: Man turned up, crossing a defensive ditch

indicators.note: crossing means the man's reversed name straddles the letter a, holding it inside
in a down clue, turned up means the man's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tom is a man's name, and a tom is also a male animal

explanation.surface: A man turned up and crossed a ditch built for defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled trench around a castle served as a protective barrier against attackers.

clue.text: Playground amenity was set up by diocese

indicators.note: by places the bishop's area beside the reversed word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, as in the Holy See

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word was is written upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: Something for children to play on was put up by the local church diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank balanced on a pivot for two children to ride up and down is standard playground equipment.

clue.text: Mischievous like Charlie, disrupting mass meeting

indicators.note: disrupting means the pieces break into the mass meeting, sitting inside it

parts.note: a rally is a large gathering of people for a cause
as means like, as in 'white as snow'
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone like Charlie is being naughty by disrupting a big public meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous rogue, so behaving like one is roguish or naughty.

clue.text: Texture of fabric you and I have spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means the contraction is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: you and I have contracts to we've

explanation.surface: A description of the texture of some cloth that you and I have talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The interlacing pattern of threads in cloth is its texture, as in a tight or loose one.

clue.text: Happen to arrive at route through mountains

parts.note: to come to a place is to arrive at it
a pass is a gap or road through a mountain range

explanation.surface: Something happens on reaching a road over the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to occur or take place, especially as foretold, as in a prophecy.

clue.text: Mean woman in bad temper, blowing top?

indicators.note: in puts the woman's name inside what is left of the temper word
blowing top means losing the first letter of the word for bad temper, with a nod to losing one's temper

parts.note: rage is a fit of bad temper
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman in a foul mood, about to lose her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' poses as unkind; it is the mathematical sense. 'blowing top' doubles as the idiom for losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a mean is the sum divided by the count, also called the typical or norm value.

clue.text: Loyalty for example accepted by coalition

indicators.note: accepted by means the abbreviation is taken inside the word for coalition

parts.note: an alliance is a coalition of parties or nations
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Faithfulness, for instance, is welcomed by a political coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithfulness owed to a sovereign, nation or cause, a synonym for being true to it.

clue.text: Cap soldiers had at Kitchener's offensive, initially?

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Headgear worn by troops in Lord Kitchener's military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener was a British field marshal; the soldiers' headgear in the surface is exactly the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall, peaked military hat with a plume was standard headwear for many nineteenth-century armies.

clue.text: Take a dekko — and see all right

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see, as in 'lo and behold'
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Have a peek and check everything is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a dekko' is British slang for have a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dekko is a quick glance, so taking one is having a peek at something.

clue.text: Asian joke involving a retired nurse once

indicators.note: involving means the joke wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a jape is a joke or prank

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the nurse's letters are read backwards

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a British nursing grade now abolished

explanation.surface: An Asian prank played on a nurse who has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, is a British grade abolished in the 1990s, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Japan is Asian, so the nationality is one example of that broader term.

clue.text: Predatory mammal some go on about?

indicators.note: about means the letters of some go on are moved around

explanation.surface: A hunting animal that some people keep talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on about' reads as nagging, but 'about' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This small carnivore of Africa and Asia hunts snakes and rodents, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Labrador, say, starts to gobble grub outside peacekeepers' party?

indicators.note: outside means the two opening letters go around the other pieces
starts to means take the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are United Nations troops
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A dog wolfing down food at a party for peacekeeping troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the two Gs either side of UNDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Labradors are bred to retrieve shot game, so one is an example of a sporting dog used in shooting.

clue.text: Drunk beginning to braise game

indicators.note: beginning to means take just the first letter of the word braise

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: Drunk from cooking: a beginner's attempt at braising game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like meat to braise; it is a game of chance.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely intoxicated, a synonym for very much the worse for drink.

clue.text: Tone down a painting technique

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or tone something down

explanation.surface: A painting method that softens a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists mixing pigment with egg yolk use this method, common before oils.

clue.text: Ornamental bobble a couple of dogs required

indicators.note: a couple of means the dog's short name is written twice

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small fluffy dog breed

explanation.surface: Two dogs are needed to make a decorative ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' is plural because two of them are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluffy ball of wool decorating a hat or cheerleader's hand is this kind of tuft.

clue.text: A teacher receiving US vocalist in Oxon town

indicators.note: receiving means a and the teacher take the singer in between them

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
Bing Crosby was an American crooner

explanation.surface: A teacher welcomes an American singer to a town in Oxfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire, an English county; this market town lies south of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: This historic market town on the Thames sits in the county of Oxfordshire.

clue.text: Clumsy writer held up by computer technology

indicators.note: held means the reversed word is held inside the abbreviation for computer technology

parts.note: IT stands for information technology

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the writer's word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An awkward author is delayed by computer problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reads as delayed, but the two words do separate jobs: 'held' contains and 'up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or competence, so a bungling, cack-handed person fits.

clue.text: Some of them market a 19th-century novel

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people sell a Victorian-era book at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's comic novel about a meddling matchmaker was published in 1815.

clue.text: Disadvantage the Spanish suffered originally

parts.note: los is a Spanish word for the, used before plural nouns

indicators.note: originally means take only the opening letter of suffered

explanation.surface: A setback that the Spanish endured at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a detriment or setback, the opposite of a gain.

clue.text: Company absorbing revolutionary statement of belief

indicators.note: absorbing means the company takes the revolutionary inside it

parts.note: a red is a communist or revolutionary

explanation.surface: A firm takes on a radical's manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'I believe', it names a creed or set of principles someone lives by.

clue.text: Skill of old wife employed in section of media

indicators.note: employed in means the two letters are put inside the media word

parts.note: the press is the newspaper section of the media
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The talent of a former spouse who once worked in journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is great ability or expertise, especially in combat or a craft.

clue.text: Unusually hot steam starts to ruin this temperature regulator

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are put in an unusual order
starts to means take the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Steam that is oddly hot begins to damage the heating control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' shuffles HOTSTEAM with R and T, the starts of 'ruin' and 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: This device switches heating or cooling on and off to keep a set warmth level.
